How’s this necessary condition trick work?

Imagine a stimulus containing solely this conditional: Q → R. This stimulus can only prove R or ~Q. Those are the only two things we can get into the provable necessary condition.

If a provable question follows, R and ~Q are the only provable correct answers. This is because R and ~Q are the only things we can get into the necessary condition.
